seed.tagline: Only the people you approve get in. Simulated users in Dev, emailed codes on every published stage, and the database enforces it.
seed.description: Adds sign-in to a project's own server (server/magic-links). A person proves their email with a six-digit code from magiclink.effortlessapi.com; the project's server finds them in the project's own table of people (there is no sign-up) and gives them a session of this app's own, with their roles and any claims you map. Every /api call then runs as that person inside the database (auth.sign_in), and row-level security decides what they see. In Dev nobody types a code: you pick any approved person and see exactly what they will see. The seed maps onto the people and roles tables the project already has, and adds AppUsers and AppRoles only when it has none. Pure SQL and Node, no extension, no runtime dependency.
seed.stack: Postgres RLS, HS256 sessions, Magic links, Express, Web components
seed.requiresInput: Nothing to type. Which table holds the people (the agent finds it) and the first admin's email.

env.MAGICLINK_TENANT_ID: The project's tenant at magiclink.effortlessapi.com, minted by the platform when the seed is added and given to every stage, Dev included. Public.

stages.dev: STAGE unset or dev. Pick your user: any active person in the table of people, no code. The session is the one a real sign-in gives that person, marked simulated.
stages.published: Any other STAGE. Email, six-digit code, session. Simulated users are refused, and a database that has once run here refuses them for good.

requiresBeforePublish.says: A magic-link tenant: MAGICLINK_TENANT_ID (set by the platform) or tenantId in magic-links.config.json.
At least one active person with the admin role in the table of people, in the rulebook's data.
The seed's two ERBCustomizations rows, current with magic-links.config.json (scripts/install.mjs).

replacements.label: Table of people
replacements.description: The rulebook table that holds the people who may sign in. Mapped to one the project already has (ERBUsers when the editor's Users and roles module is on; Members, Staff, Volunteers...). AppUsers is added only when nothing maps.

replacements.label: Person's key
replacements.description: The field that identifies a person (usually the table's first field). Becomes the session's sub, which policies read as app.user_key(). Blank: the email is the key.

replacements.label: Email field
replacements.description: The field matched, case-blind, against the email a person proves. When two rows share an address, the active one wins.

replacements.label: Name field
replacements.description: Shown in the app and in Dev's pick-your-user list. Blank: the email.

replacements.label: Active field
replacements.description: A boolean: false keeps the row but stops the person at once, open sessions included. Start it with ! for a field that is true when the person is NOT allowed (!IsDisabled). Blank: every row is active. A status text field (Status = Active) is mapped through a calculated boolean field added to the rulebook, with the person's yes.

replacements.label: Role field
replacements.description: The field on the table of people holding the person's role: a link to the roles table, or text (comma-separate for several). Blank when roles come from a table that links people to roles (userRolesTable).

replacements.label: Roles table
replacements.description: The table of roles, offered in the setup screen's pickers. AppRoles is added only when the project has none and the roles are not plain text. Blank: roles are plain text.

replacements.label: Role's key
replacements.description: The roles table's key: the value a person's role field holds, and the value the session's roles carry.

replacements.label: People-to-roles table
replacements.description: Set when a person can hold several roles through a table of grants (the rulebook has no many-to-many). Blank: roleField.

replacements.label: Grant's person
replacements.description: On the people-to-roles table: the field pointing at the person (holds their key).

replacements.label: Grant's role
replacements.description: On the people-to-roles table: the field holding the role.

replacements.label: Admin role
replacements.description: The role that may open the setup screen, manage people and use the generated API's schema routes. At least one active person must hold it before the first publish.

replacements.label: Session length (hours)
replacements.description: How long a session lasts before the person proves their email again. Deactivating someone stops their session at once whatever this says.

replacements.label: Extra claims
replacements.description: More facts from the person's row carried in the session, claim=Field, comma-separated. Policies read them as app.claim('company'), the app from /api/auth/session.

replacements.label: Paths that need a session
replacements.description: Path prefixes the project's server refuses (401) without a session, comma-separated. /api/auth and /api/magic-links are always open.

replacements.label: Open paths
replacements.description: Path prefixes inside the protected ones that stay open (health checks, webhooks that sign their own requests), comma-separated.

replacements.label: Cookie name
replacements.description: The HttpOnly cookie that holds the session on the app's own address.

replacements.label: Magic-link tenant
replacements.description: The project's tenant at magiclink.effortlessapi.com. Leave blank on Effortless: the platform mints one and sets MAGICLINK_TENANT_ID, which wins. Elsewhere, create one at magiclink.effortlessapi.com and put its id here. Public.

replacements.label: Magic-links service
replacements.description: Where the tenant lives. MAGICLINK_BASE_URL in the environment wins.
